h1: The 5 Best 56V Leaf Blowers of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 5 genuine 56V cordless leaf blowers scored on airflow, wet-leaf power and platform, from EGO Power+ at 880 CFM to Echo eFORCE.
summary: The EGO Power+ at 880 CFM is the strongest 56V blower here and the one to buy for wet leaves and caked debris. The 765 CFM EGO is the better value if you do not need the extra push. The 615 CFM EGO is the entry price for the platform, and the 530 CFM EGO suits light cleanup. If you already own Echo eFORCE 56V batteries, the Echo model slots straight into that system.
intro: A 56V blower is a platform decision as much as a tool choice. Both EGO and Echo run their outdoor tools on 56V battery packs, and a blower is often the first purchase before a mower, trimmer or chainsaw joins the family. Buy a blower with the wrong battery and every future tool costs more.

That is why this list covers only genuine 56V models and ranks them mostly on airflow in cubic feet per minute, the number that decides whether a blower moves wet leaves or just stirs them. Scores follow spec sheets and yard-owner reports, and we checked the listing for battery and charger details.

products.name: EGO Power+ Cordless Electric Leaf Blower (880 CFM)
products.verdict: Up to 880 CFM and turbo speeds to 200 MPH. The strongest handheld here.
products.description:
This EGO Power+ is the most powerful blower in the group, rated for up to 880 CFM with a turbo mode that reaches speeds up to 200 MPH. That kind of airflow is what lifts wet leaves and caked debris off the ground instead of just rolling them around.

It costs the most and is worth the premium if you have a large yard or lots of trees. Next to the 765 CFM EGO, you gain a noticeable push at the top end for a higher price. Check the listing carefully, because exact model and included accessories can differ between sellers.

Buy it if you have a big lot, heavy leaf drop or wet autumn weather. For a small yard it is more blower than you need.
cons: More than a small yard needs
products.idealFor: Large yards and heavy, wet leaf drop.
products.skipIf: You have a small yard or light debris.

products.name: EGO POWER+ Cordless Electric Leaf Blower (765 CFM)
products.verdict: 765 CFM and a 200 MPH turbo, enough for wet leaves at a lower price than the 880.
products.description:
The 765 CFM model offers the same turbo ceiling of up to 200 MPH as the flagship but with a little less airflow. In practice it still handles wet leaves and caked debris, which is the real test for a cordless blower.

It ranks second because it keeps most of the performance for less money, and it has a long record among buyers of the EGO line. Against the 615 CFM version you get a clear step in power. You give up only the last bit of push the 880 offers.

A good choice for average to large yards where you want strong performance without paying the top price.
products.idealFor: Medium to large yards that want strong power for less.
products.skipIf: You want the absolute maximum airflow.

products.name: EGO POWER+ Cordless Electric Leaf Blower (615 CFM)
products.verdict: 615 CFM covers typical leaf cleanup, and it is the most affordable way into EGO's 56V platform.
products.description:
The 615 CFM blower is the cheapest of the EGO picks here, yet it covers normal leaf and debris cleanup on an average lot. Battery power means no gas, no pull cord and no maintenance routine.

It ranks below the 765 CFM because wet leaves and compacted piles ask for more airflow than it offers. Compared with the 530 CFM it gives a meaningful lift in power for a small premium.

Best for a typical suburban yard where the goal is a reliable blower on the 56V platform without overspending.
products.idealFor: Average yards that want a dependable first 56V tool.
products.skipIf: You regularly clear wet, matted leaves.

products.name: Echo eFORCE 56V 151 MPH 526 CFM Cordless Handheld Blower
products.verdict: 151 MPH and 526 CFM on the Echo eFORCE 56V platform from a pro-focused brand.
products.description:
The Echo eFORCE is a handheld on Echo's own 56V platform, listed at 151 MPH and 526 CFM. Echo is known for professional-grade outdoor equipment, and this blower is aimed at owners who want that brand's batteries across their tools.

It ranks lower purely on numbers: 526 CFM is on the low side next to the stronger EGO blowers, and it is a newer listing with less history. Its argument is the platform rather than the power. Verify the listing for what is included.

Choose it if you already own Echo eFORCE tools or prefer the brand, otherwise the EGO blowers offer more airflow.
products.idealFor: Owners of Echo eFORCE batteries and tools.
products.skipIf: You are choosing a platform and want maximum airflow.

products.name: EGO POWER+ Cordless Electric Leaf Blower (530 CFM)
products.verdict: The most modest airflow of the EGO picks, but fine for patios and light leaves.
products.description:
At 530 CFM this is the gentlest EGO here, aimed at lighter cleanup such as patios, decks, driveways and dry leaves. It has a long track record on the platform and skips gas fumes and maintenance entirely.

It ranks last because airflow is the main thing a blower is for, and it has the least. Wet piles and compacted debris are beyond it, which is where the 615 and 765 CFM models earn their cost.

Only worth it for small yards, hard surfaces and dry debris.
pros: Long track record on the platform
cons: Lowest airflow in the EGO group
products.idealFor: Small yards and hard surfaces with dry debris.
products.skipIf: You have trees that drop heavy, wet leaves.

methodology.title: Genuine 56V platform
methodology.description: We only kept blowers that run on a true 56V battery system, because mixing platforms is the most common buying mistake in this category.

methodology.title: Airflow in CFM
methodology.description: Cubic feet per minute was the main ranking input, since it decides whether a blower moves wet material.

methodology.title: Turbo and speed
methodology.description: Air speed in MPH and turbo modes were compared as a second measure of how much work each blower does at the nozzle.

methodology.title: Platform value
methodology.description: We weighed what each battery system offers for future tools, not just the blower itself.

methodology.title: Listing clarity
methodology.description: Listings that make battery and charger inclusion unclear were noted, since some tools ship as bare units.

whatMatters.factor: CFM is the number to read first
whatMatters.detail: CFM measures air volume, and it is what moves a pile of leaves. MPH measures air speed, which helps loosen stuck debris. Wet leaves need high CFM. For a typical yard, 600 to 800 CFM is a comfortable range; below 550 CFM is for light work only.

Some 56V tools are sold bare, with no battery or charger. A blower without a pack is useless on its own. Read the listing title and the included items before ordering, and confirm the kit says battery and charger.

whatMatters.factor: Pick the platform before the tool
whatMatters.detail: EGO and Echo use different 56V batteries that do not interchange. If you already own one brand's mower or trimmer, buying the same brand's blower lets you share batteries. Starting fresh, EGO has the larger range among the picks here.
Turbo mode drains a battery fast. A larger amp-hour pack runs longer, but adds weight. If your yard takes 20 minutes, a standard pack suffices; for larger jobs plan for a bigger pack or a spare.
A blower you carry for 30 minutes needs to feel balanced. Handheld models vary in weight, and heavier ones tire the wrist. Check the listed weight and the battery's added mass before buying.

cards.text: At least 700 CFM, a turbo button for stuck piles, and a battery that lasts through a full cleanup session.

faq.q: Are EGO and Echo 56V batteries interchangeable?
faq.a: No. They are separate platforms that share only a voltage label. Buy the blower that matches the batteries you already own.

faq.q: How many CFM do I need?
faq.a: For a typical yard 600 to 800 CFM is comfortable. Wet leaves call for the 765 or 880 CFM EGO, and light cleanup can use the 530 CFM.

faq.q: Does the blower come with a battery?
faq.a: Not always. Some 56V tools are sold bare. Read the listing for 'battery and charger included' before you order.
It boosts airflow temporarily to loosen stubborn debris, but drains the battery faster. Use it in short bursts.

faq.q: Can a cordless blower replace a gas one?
faq.a: For most home yards, yes. The 880 CFM EGO Power+ handles wet leaves that used to need gas, without fumes or a pull cord.

faq.q: Is the Echo eFORCE worth buying on its own?
faq.a: Only if you want the Echo platform. On airflow alone it trails the 765 and 880 CFM EGO models.

finalTake: The EGO Power+ 880 CFM is the best 56V leaf blower for anyone with a large yard or wet leaves. The 765 CFM EGO gives most of that power for less, and the 615 CFM EGO is the sensible entry point. Pick the Echo eFORCE only if you are already in the Echo battery system.
